summary:
NERIA (Nature's Evidence for Regional Investigation and Analysis) is an interactive web platform that turns NASA Earth observation data into guided investigations of environmental change — for any location on Earth, in English and Spanish, without coding.

It tackles a common trap: drawing conclusions from a short, conveniently chosen window of years. Near Santiago del Estero, Argentina, five years of NASA POWER / MERRA-2 data show +3.53 °C per decade; with 45 years (1981–2025) the trend is −0.06 °C per decade and the verdict changes.

Users first register a prediction, then widen the analysis period with a slider. The tool answers the challenge’s key questions — what is changing, where, how much, and whether it is significant. NERIA applies robust statistics (Theil–Sen slopes, block bootstrap confidence intervals, Mann–Kendall and false-discovery-rate control) and returns a clear verdict with its uncertainty, explained in simple language. A 3D globe, charts and an assistant guide each step, and every result includes its data sources, method and a SHA-256 fingerprint for verification.

NERIA makes scientific analysis accessible to students, journalists, researchers and communities, helping them recognize data limitations and base decisions about water, agriculture and energy on verifiable, long-term evidence.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

NERIA (Nature's Evidence for Regional Investigation and Analysis) is an open-science web tool that tests climate claims against NASA data. It targets a common trap: drawing conclusions from a short, conveniently chosen window of years. Near Santiago del Estero, Argentina, five years of NASA POWER / MERRA-2 air temperature (2021–2025) show +3.53 °C per decade. Widen the window to 45 years (1981–2025) and the Theil–Sen slope is −0.06 °C per decade, with a 95% confidence interval of [−0.23, +0.10]: the verdict changes. That does not prove there is no change — it shows five years were not enough.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Predict first: the user registers a hypothesis ("goes up", "goes down", "not enough to conclude") before seeing any result, to avoid hindsight bias.

2. Widen the window: a slider moves from 5 to 10, 20, 30 and 45 years while the final year stays fixed at 2025.

3. Read the verdict: each series gets one of five protocol verdicts (supported trend, signal to investigate, method-sensitive, short window: exploratory, insufficient data), based on a Theil–Sen slope, OLS with HAC errors, a residual block bootstrap 95% CI, the Mann–Kendall test with Hamed–Rao correction, and Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate control (q). Windows shorter than 20 years are labeled exploratory.

4. Compare places: case file 2 compares annual rainfall in central Chile (−106.4 mm/yr per decade, q = 0.001, supported trend) and northern Europe (−37.9 mm/yr per decade, signal to investigate). We expected opposite directions and did not find them — NERIA shows the real result, not the one we wanted.

5. Explore anywhere: a four-step assistant (topic → variables → location → analysis) with nine topics, a 3D Planetary Observatory and a global explorer let users investigate any place on Earth; the map shows the exact NASA grid cell (~0.5° × 0.625°), not a provincial average.

6. Verify and cite: every case file shows its method version, uncertainty and the SHA-256 fingerprint of the raw data, and can be exported (JSON, CSV, PDF) or copied as a verifiable citation.

NASA DATA AND OTHER SOURCES

• NASA POWER / MERRA-2 (NASA LaRC, NASA GMAO): monthly T2M, PRECTOTCORR and other variables, 1981–2025 — the long series behind every trend.

• NASA GES DISC: Giovanni (GPM IMERG v07) and GLDAS Noah L4 (v2.1).

• NASA LP DAAC: AppEEARS (MODIS/Terra MOD11A1 v6.1, 1 km land surface temperature).

• NASA Earth Observatory: Blue Marble and Black Marble imagery for the 3D globe.

• NOAA NCEI GHCN-Daily stations to contrast grid cells with ground measurements, and Meteomatics for 30-day recent weather — always shown separately and never blended into climate trends.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

NERIA turns NASA Earth-observation data into guided, honest investigations that anyone can run in a browser, in English or Spanish, without installing software. It is designed for secondary and university classrooms, newsrooms checking climate headlines, and communities anywhere in the world — including our own region, the Gran Chaco — that need long-term evidence instead of short-term impressions. Its goal is to make "how many years are enough?" a reflex before any climate conclusion is shared or acted upon.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

• Data and statistics pipeline: Python (NumPy, pandas, SciPy, statsmodels, pymannkendall, httpx), with pinned dependencies and automated tests (55 pytest tests).

• Web app: TypeScript, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Three.js (3D globe and observatory), GSAP (motion), Plotly (charts), with 121 Vitest tests.

• Hosting and backend: Amazon Web Services (Ubuntu server with Apache) and a Node.js API with SQLite for live source checks, custom places and the recent-weather layer; all credentials stay server-side.

• Content: bilingual interface (ES/EN), an accessible data table as an alternative to the charts, and reproducible case files generated from the pipeline.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

Instead of showing a chart and asking users to trust it, NERIA turns climate analysis into a detective game with a scientific protocol: you bet first, the evidence answers, and the tool openly reports when our own hypothesis fails. The window slider makes cherry-picking visible in seconds, and the 3D observatory connects each local verdict to its place on the planet.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

• Scientific honesty: uncertainty is always visible, non-significant results are never presented as "proof of no change", and no causal claims are made.

• Spatial honesty: each value represents one NASA grid cell, labeled as such.

• Multiple comparisons: FDR control (q) when several series are tested.

• Reproducibility: fixed method version, SHA-256 fingerprints and links to each original query.

• Separation of weather and climate: 30-day weather data never enters trend calculations.

• Accessibility and reach: works in any browser, on desktop and mobile, in two languages, for any location worldwide.

• Transparent use of AI: AI assistants helped with code and texts, but every number and verdict comes from the reproducible statistical pipeline, never from AI.
